subject: Discovery recap & procurement next steps — FinLogix evaluation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@finlogix.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlogix.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-04T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery recap & procurement next steps

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

High-level pain points you outlined:
- Large batch jobs and interactive search features are suffering inconsistent latency under load; current infra struggles with spikes.
- Cost growth from token generation for nightly processing is hitting the forecasting threshold.
- Security/compliance gates: SOC2 audit coming Q1, and procurement needs clarity around data residency and audit logs.

Current stack / constraints:
- FinLogix runs inference on a mix of cloud-managed endpoints and a small on-prem cluster for PHI workloads (K8s + private GPUs).
- Primary frameworks: PyTorch & Triton-based endpoints; inference requests come through an API gateway.

Success criteria for a pilot (what would make this successful):
1) Reduce 95th percentile latency for interactive requests by >40% under production-like traffic.
2) Demonstrate predictable per-token/unit economics with a committed pilot.
3) Show integration path for private/VPC deployment for PHI workloads and basic audit logging for SOC2 evidence.

Decision process & stakeholders (as discussed):
- Technical evaluation: Evan (POC owner) + Priya (product lead) + Sean (SE) for appendix.
- Procurement/legal: Maya Singh (contract lead) + FinLogix procurement team.
- Executive approval: CTO/VP Product after procurement review.
- Target decision window: ~mid-December (aiming for sign/commit by 2025-12-15).

Initial commercial guardrails (we discussed ranges):
- Pilot options: 3-month committed pilot (preferred for predictability) vs pay-as-you-go evaluation.
- Ballpark committed pilot budget you mentioned: in the $15k–$35k range for an initial scope — we will refine after SE sizing.
- Preferred contract vehicle: Purchase Order or short term SaaS SOW with renewal options.

Next steps (owner / timing):
1) I’ll route a technical appendix and a draft SOW / pricing band by EOD 2025-11-06 (Marissa).
2) Sean to provide capacity/latency sizing and suggested pilot configuration (by 2025-11-06).
3) Evan to introduce procurement contact (Maya) to the thread if comfortable (you said you would).
4) Schedule procurement + technical alignment meeting week of Nov 17 — calendar invite once we confirm attendees.

Attachments: referenced one-pager (see deck we will send).

Thanks — happy to adjust if I missed something.

Best,
Marissa Cole

- Procurement: please include Maya Singh (legal/procurement) on future SOW/pricing threads. I’ve cc'd her on a separate email; bringing her fully into the thread now (maya@legalbridge.com).
- SOC2 / data residency: we will need a SOC2 report and confirmation of log retention options for audit evidence.
- Pilot scope: the $15k–$35k range sounds reasonable as an initial guardrail; we prefer to see what a 3-month committed pilot looks like day-to-day (throughput & cost tradeoffs).
- Timeline: procurement typically requires 2–3 weeks for review once a SOW is shared. Our internal exec window aligns with mid-December.

Requests:
1) Please send a short SOW and ballpark committed vs pay-as-you-go pricing bands.
2) Sean — when you have a moment, can you outline the minimal pilot configuration (vCPU/GPU estimate, expected latency SLOs, KV/prefix cache options) so we can compare to current infra?

I’ll coordinate Maya’s calendar for a procurement sync once we have those docs.

Thanks,

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & procurement next steps — Tech appendix + next steps

Hi all — thanks for the helpful discussion. Attaching a short deck and a draft SOW for FinLogix (see attachments: redwood-deck.pdf, SOW-draft.docx). Summary / next steps below.

Technical appendix (high-level):
- Deployment options: hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved pool (predictable throughput), Private VPC (for PHI). We can run the pilot in Hosted mode with a private VPC tunnel for audit logs if you prefer.
- Performance: for the interactive search workload described, we project ~40–60% reduction in 95p latency compared to your current endpoints using continual batching + KV caching; exact numbers depend on sequence length distribution.
- Sizing (pilot): 1 x A100-equivalent for model serving + modest CPU workers for routing should cover an MVP 3-month pilot for the traffic profile discussed. If you need a more conservative buffer, we recommend 2 x GPU.
- Observability & evidence: we can provide request-level traces, token cost breakdowns, and a retention window for audit logs to satisfy SOC2 reviewers.

Commercial guardrails (proposal):
- Pilot: 3 months, committed credits in the $20k–$30k range (negotiable based on required buffer and SLA).
- Pay-as-you-go option: available for evaluation but expect higher unit costs; we’ll include both bands in the SOW.

Next steps / actions:
1) Marissa: finalize SOW template and send to Maya & Evan (target: EOD 2025-11-06).
2) FinLogix: confirm procurement contact and preferred contracting vehicle (PO vs MSA + SOW).
3) Schedule combined procurement + technical sync the week of Nov 17 (Marissa to send a poll).

I’ve included a short pricing appendix in the SOW for committed vs on-demand pricing and a proposed pilot acceptance criteria.

Calendar: https://cal.com/marissa/redwood-finlogix

Happy to jump on a follow-up to walk through the appendix.

Regards,
